page.title: Strategies
page.purpose: Show the strategy registry and the conformance matrix: which capability tier each strategy actually satisfies, verified rather than declared.

priorities.statement: Declared capability and verified capability are shown as separate columns.
priorities.notes: Collapsing them makes every strategy self-certifying, which is exactly what the two-seam design exists to prevent.

priorities.statement: A strategy that has never been verified is marked unverified, not assumed passing.
priorities.notes: Never-probed and probed-to-zero are different findings and must never render alike.

priorities.statement: Each strategy shows which flow step kinds it can execute.
priorities.notes: The capability set is the input; the executable step vocabulary is what an author actually needs.

states.description: The registry with at least one verified strategy.
No strategies registered; explains that a strategy is added by implementing the floor and passing the suite.
Some strategies are verified and others have never been run; the mixture is the normal state.
A conformance result predates the current strategy registration; shown as stale rather than current.
The registry request failed; the page says so rather than presenting an empty registry.
A strategy whose declaration was fully proven by probing, with an empty delta.
A registered strategy that has never been run through the conformance suite. Not a passing state.
A non-empty delta: the strategy declared a capability the probe could not prove.

elements.name: Conformance
elements.description: One row per strategy with floor conformance, declared count, probed count, and delta.

elements.name: Probed
elements.description: What verification actually proved. Never merged with the declared column.
Per-capability explanation of what was declared but unprovable, including the missing prerequisite.
Floor conformance — the only hard gate. Pass or fail, with no partial value.
Marks a strategy that has never been run through the suite. Renders as an em dash, never a zero.

elements.name: Executable steps
elements.description: The flow step kinds this strategy can run, derived from its probed capability set.
Matched profiles. Informational only — the capability set is the authority.

elements.name: Verify
elements.description: Run the conformance suite against a strategy.
Empty-state explanation of how a strategy joins the registry.

claims.statement: Declared capability and probed capability are presented as separate columns.
claims.rationale: Priority 1 and D-002. Merging them makes every strategy self-certifying, which is the failure the two-seam design exists to prevent.

claims.statement: A strategy that has never been verified is perceivably different from one verified to have no optional capabilities.
claims.rationale: Priority 2. ios-mirror legitimately probes to zero optional capabilities; that is a finding. A never-run suite is an absence of data. Rendering both as 0 destroys the distinction.

claims.statement: The declared-but-unprovable delta is presented directly rather than left for the reader to derive.
claims.rationale: The delta is the finding the conformance suite exists to produce. Requiring subtraction to see it buries the page's whole output.

claims.statement: Floor conformance is shown as a pass-or-fail outcome with no intermediate value.
claims.rationale: D-001. A component that does not implement all three floor operations is not a strategy; a partial floor is not a meaningful state.

claims.statement: Each strategy shows which flow step kinds it can execute.
claims.rationale: Priority 3. The capability set is the input a flow author cannot use directly; the executable step vocabulary is what they actually need.

claims.statement: A matched profile is presented as a summary of probe results rather than as an authority in its own right.
claims.rationale: capabilities.md is explicit that profiles carry no authority and that matching none is not a failure. A profile badge given more visual weight than the capability set would invert that.

claims.statement: The empty state explains that a strategy joins the registry by implementing the floor and passing the suite.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-002 promises that adding a strategy requires no engine change; the empty state is where that promise is discoverable.
